acceptanceCriteria: A proposed spec defines the note record, anchors, revision pinning, STALE rules, delivery, write/supersede/retract path, byte caps, secret screening and non-goals, with numbered requirements and rollback.
A note can be recorded with anchors and provenance; supersede and retract keep immutable history.
A note whose path anchor's content changed since its pinned revision reads as STALE; unchanged anchors read as CURRENT; an anchor that cannot be resolved reads as UNKNOWN, never CURRENT.
Claim output (or an explicit read) delivers the notes whose anchors intersect the claimed ticket's declared paths, as a compact projection under a byte cap with omitted counts; reads never mutate.
Note text is secret-screened on write and is labelled untrusted agent-authored data on delivery; notes never feed ranking, evidence or authority.
body: Owner request https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/655 (2026-10-07). Sessions rediscover the same how-to knowledge (how to reach a screen, which helper does a task, required setup, stable selectors) per ticket because it stays in the ticket's own notes. Adopters work around this with keyword-matched local stores that have no staleness, no anchor binding and no provenance. Ask: a Corvint-owned cross-ticket note record; each note binds to anchors (source paths or symbols, route or flow IDs, test files) pinned to the revision it was written at; a note becomes STALE when an anchor's content changes and stays marked until re-confirmed or superseded; notes whose anchors intersect a ticket's scope are delivered on claim (and later through corvint_query) as a byte-capped compact projection; writes record attempt, generation and evidence path as provenance, and supersede or retract with a reason over immutable history (as operator notes, ON-V0). Optional promotion of repeatedly confirmed notes through skill-export (LTA-V0-006).
